cues.en: In the last chapter, you and I started to step through the internal workings of a transformer. This is one of the key pieces of technology inside large language models and a lot of other tools in the modern wave of AI.
cues.zh: 在上一章中，你和我开始一步步剖析 Transformer 的内部工作原理。这是大语言模型以及现代 AI 浪潮中许多其他工具的核心技术之一。

cues.en: It first hit the scene in a now famous 2017 paper called attention is all you need. And in this chapter, you and I will dig into what this attention mechanism is, visualizing how it processes data.
cues.zh: 它首次亮相是在 2017 年那篇如今已名声大噪的论文《Attention Is All You Need》中。在这一章里，你和我将深入探讨什么是注意力机制，并将其处理数据的方式可视化。

cues.en: As a quick recap, here's the important context I want you to have in mind. The goal of the model that you and I are studying is to take in a piece of text and predict what word comes next.
cues.zh: 简单回顾一下，这是我希望你记住的重要背景：你和我正在研究的这个模型，其目标是输入一段文本，然后预测接下来会出现什么词。

cues.en: The input text is broken up into little pieces that we call tokens,
cues.zh: 输入文本会被拆分成我们称之为 Token 的小片段，

cues.en: and these are very often words or pieces of words. But just to make the examples in this video easier for you and me to think about, let's simplify by pretending that tokens are always just words.
cues.zh: 它们通常是词或词的一部分。但为了让你和我更容易思考本视频中的例子，我们简化一下，假装 Token 总是代表完整的词。

cues.en: The first step in a transformer is to associate each token with a high dimensional vector,
cues.zh: Transformer 的第一步是将每个 Token 与一个高维向量关联起来，

cues.en: what we call its embedding.
cues.zh: 也就是我们所说的嵌入（embedding）。

cues.en: Now the most important idea I want you to have in mind is how directions in this high dimensional space of all possible embeddings
cues.zh: 现在，我希望你记住的最核心概念是，所有可能嵌入组成的高维空间中的方向，

cues.en: can correspond with semantic meaning. In the last chapter, we saw an example for how direction can correspond to gender in the sense that adding a certain step in this space can take you from the embedding of a masculine noun to the embedding of the corresponding feminine noun. That's just one example you could imagine how many other directions in this high dimensional space could correspond to numerous other aspects of a word's meaning.
cues.zh: 是如何与语义相对应的。在上一章中，我们看到了一个方向如何对应性别的例子：在这个空间中加上某个特定的位移，就能从一个阳性名词的嵌入变换到对应的阴性名词的嵌入。这只是一个例子，你可以想象这个高维空间中的许多其他方向如何对应着词义的众多其他方面。

cues.en: The aim of a transformer is to progressively adjust these embeddings so that they don't merely encode an individual word,
cues.zh: Transformer 的目标是逐步调整这些嵌入，使得它们不仅能编码单个单词，

cues.en: but instead they bake in some much much richer contextual meaning.
cues.zh: 而是融入丰富得多的上下文含义。

cues.en: I should say upfront that a lot of people find the attention mechanism, this key piece in a transformer,
cues.zh: 我先说明一下，很多人都会觉得注意力机制这个 Transformer 的核心部件，

cues.en: very confusing. So don't worry if it takes some time for things to sink in.
cues.zh: 非常令人困惑。所以如果需要花点时间才能完全理解，也不用担心。

cues.en: I think that before we dive into the computational details and all the matrix multiplications,
cues.zh: 我想在我们深入计算细节和各种矩阵乘法之前，

cues.en: it's worth thinking about a couple examples for the kind of behavior that we want attention to enable.
cues.zh: 我们先思考几个例子，看看我们希望注意力机制实现什么样的效果。

cues.en: Consider the phrases American true mole, one mole of carbon dioxide,
cues.zh: 考虑这几个短语：美洲鼹鼠、一摩尔二氧化碳、

cues.en: and take a biopsy of the mole. You and I know that the word mole has different meanings in each one of these based on the context.
cues.zh: 以及对痣进行活检。你我都清楚，基于上下文，单词 mole 在这几个例子中有着不同的含义。

cues.en: But after the first step of a transformer, the one that breaks up the text and associates each token with a vector,
cues.zh: 但在 Transformer 的第一步之后，也就是那个将文本分词并把每个 token 与向量关联起来的步骤，

cues.en: the vector that's associated with mole would be the same in all three of these cases because this initial token embedding is effectively a lookup table with no reference to the context.
cues.zh: 在所有这三种情况下，与 mole 关联的向量都是完全一样的，因为这个初始的 token 嵌入本质上只是一个不考虑上下文的查找表。

cues.en: It's only in the next step of the transformer that the surrounding embeddings have the chance to pass information into this one.
cues.zh: 直到 Transformer 的下一步，周围的嵌入才有机会将信息传递给当前这个嵌入。

cues.en: The picture you might have in mind is that there are multiple distinct directions in this embedding space encoding the multiple distinct meanings of the word mole, and that a well trained attention block calculates
cues.zh: 你脑海中浮现的画面可能是：在这个嵌入空间中存在多个不同的方向，分别编码了 mole 这个词的多种不同含义，而一个训练良好的注意力块会根据上下文计算出

cues.en: what you need to add to the generic embedding to move it to one of these more specific directions as a function of the context.
cues.zh: 需要向通用的嵌入添加什么内容，才能将其移动到这些更具体的方向之一。

cues.en: To take another example, consider the embedding of the word tower.
cues.zh: 再举个例子，考虑单词 tower 的嵌入。

cues.en: This is presumably some very generic nonspecific
cues.zh: 这很可能是一个非常通用、不具体的

cues.en: direction in the space associated with lots of other large tall nouns.
cues.zh: 空间方向，与许多其他又大又高的名词相关联。

cues.en: If this word was immediately preceded by eiffel,
cues.zh: 如果这个词的前面紧挨着 eiffel，

cues.en: you could imagine wanting the mechanism to update this vector so that it points in a direction that more specifically encodes the Eiffel Tower, maybe correlated with vectors associated with Paris and France and things made of steel.
cues.zh: 你可以想象，我们希望这个机制能够更新这个向量，使其指向一个更具体地编码埃菲尔铁塔的方向，或许与和巴黎、法国以及钢制物品相关的向量产生关联。

cues.en: If it was also preceded by the word miniature,
cues.zh: 如果它的前面还有 miniature 这个词，

cues.en: then the vector should be updated even further so that it no longer correlates with large tall things.
cues.zh: 那么这个向量就应该被进一步更新，从而不再与又大又高的事物相关联。

cues.en: More generally than just refining the meaning of a word, the attention block allows the model to move information encoded in one embedding to that of another, potentially ones that are quite far away and potentially with information that's much richer than just a single word.
cues.zh: 比单纯细化词义更普遍的是，注意力模块允许模型将编码在一个嵌入中的信息转移到另一个嵌入中，这些嵌入可能相距甚远，并且所包含的信息可能远比单个词丰富得多。

cues.en: What we saw in the last chapter was how after all of the vectors flow through the network, including many different attention blocks,
cues.zh: 我们在上一章中看到的是，在所有向量流经网络（包括许多不同的注意力模块）之后，

cues.en: the computation that you perform to produce a prediction of the next token
cues.zh: 你为了生成下一个 token 的预测而执行的计算，

cues.en: is entirely
cues.zh: 完全

cues.en: a function of the last vector in the sequence.
cues.zh: 是序列中最后一个向量的函数。

cues.en: So imagine, for example, that the text you input is most of an entire mystery novel all the way up to a point near the end, which reads, therefore, the murderer was.
cues.zh: 所以想象一下，举个例子，你输入的文本是一整部悬疑小说的大部分内容，一直延伸到接近结尾的一个地方，上面写着：“因此，凶手是”。

cues.en: If the model's going to accurately predict the next word, that final vector in the sequence, which began its life simply embedding the word was,
cues.zh: 如果模型要准确预测下一个词，那么序列中的最后一个向量——它最初只是对单词本身进行的嵌入——

cues.en: will have to have been updated by all of the attention blocks to represent much much more than any individual word,
cues.zh: 必须经过所有 attention block 的更新，从而代表远超任何单个词的含义，

cues.en: somehow encoding all of the information from the full context window that's relevant to predicting the next word.
cues.zh: 从而以某种方式编码来自完整上下文窗口中所有与预测下一个词相关的信息。

cues.en: To step through the computations though, let's take a much simpler example. Imagine that the input includes the phrase, a fluffy blue creature roamed the verdant forest. And for the moment, suppose that the only type of update that we care about is having the adjectives
cues.zh: 不过，为了逐步了解这些计算过程，我们来看一个简单得多的例子。想象一下输入中包含这样一句话：一只毛茸茸的蓝色生物在苍翠的森林里游荡。现在，假设我们唯一关心的更新类型是让形容词

cues.en: adjust the meanings of their corresponding nouns.
cues.zh: 去调整它们对应名词的含义。

cues.en: What I'm about to describe is what we would call a single head of attention.
cues.zh: 我接下来要描述的就是我们所说的单头 attention。

cues.en: And later, we will see how the attention block consists of many different heads run-in parallel.
cues.zh: 稍后，我们将看到 attention block 是由多个并行运行的不同 head 组成的。

cues.en: Again, the initial embedding for each word is some high dimensional vector that only encodes the meaning of that particular word with no context.
cues.zh: 同样，每个词最初的 embedding 都是一个高维向量，它只编码了该特定词的含义，而没有任何上下文。

cues.en: Actually, that's not quite true. They also encode the position of the word. There's a lot more to say about the specific way the positions are encoded,
cues.zh: 其实，这不太准确。它们还编码了词的位置。关于位置编码的具体方式，还有很多内容要讲，

cues.en: but right now, all you need to know is that the entries of this vector are enough to tell you both what the word is and where it exists in the context.
cues.zh: 但现在，你只需要知道这个向量中的各项足以告诉你这个词是什么，以及它在上下文中处于什么位置。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and denote these embeddings with the letter e.
cues.zh: 我们把这些嵌入表示记为字母 e。

cues.en: The goal is to have a series of computations produce a new refined set of embeddings where, for example, those corresponding to the nouns have ingested the meaning from their corresponding adjectives.
cues.zh: 目标是通过一系列计算，产生一组新的、精炼的嵌入。例如，让名词对应的嵌入吸收其对应形容词的含义。

cues.en: And playing the deep learning game, we want most of the computations involved to look like matrix vector products where the matrices are full of tunable weights, things that the model will learn based on data.
cues.zh: 在深度学习的常规套路中，我们希望大部分相关的计算都表现为矩阵与向量的乘积，其中矩阵里充满了可调的权重——也就是模型会基于数据去学习的参数。

cues.en: To be clear, I'm making up this example of adjectives updating nouns just to illustrate the type of behavior that you could imagine an intention had doing.
cues.zh: 需要说明的是，我编造这个“形容词更新名词”的例子，只是为了说明你可以想象注意力机制（attention）会实现的那种行为。

cues.en: As with so much deep learning, the true behavior is much harder to parse because it's based on tweaking and tuning a huge number of parameters to minimize some cost function.
cues.zh: 正如很多深度学习场景一样，真实的表现要难解析得多，因为它是基于对海量参数的微调和优化，来最小化某种成本函数的。

cues.en: It's just that as we step through all of the different matrices filled with parameters that are involved in this process, I think it's really helpful to have an imagined example of something that it could be doing to help keep it all more concrete.
cues.zh: 不过，在我们遍历参与这个过程的所有装满参数的矩阵时，我觉得如果能脑补一个它可能在做什么的具体例子，会对理解大有帮助。

cues.en: For the first step of this process, you might imagine each noun, like creature,
cues.zh: 在这个过程的第一步，你可以想象每个名词（比如“creature”），

cues.en: asking the question, hey, are there any adjectives sitting in front of me? And for the words fluffy and blue to each be able to answer, yeah, I'm an adjective and I'm in that position.
cues.zh: 都会发出这样一个疑问：“嘿，我前面有形容词吗？”然后“fluffy”和“blue”这两个词都能回应：“有啊，我是形容词，而且就在那个位置。”

cues.en: That question is somehow encoded as yet another vector, another list of numbers,
cues.zh: 那个问题在某种程度上被编码成了另一个向量，另一串数字，

cues.en: which we call the query for this word.
cues.zh: 我们称之为这个词的查询。

cues.en: This query vector though has a much smaller dimension than the embedding vector, say a 128.
cues.zh: 不过这个查询向量的维度比嵌入向量小得多，比如说是 128 维。

cues.en: Computing this query looks like taking a certain matrix, which I'll label w q, and multiplying it by the embedding.
cues.zh: 计算这个查询，看起来就是取某个矩阵——我把它标记为 w q——然后乘以嵌入。

cues.en: Compressing things a bit, let's write that query vector as q. And then anytime you see me put a matrix next to an arrow like this one, it's meant to represent that multiplying this matrix by the vector at the arrow's start gives you the vector at the arrow's end.
cues.zh: 稍微压缩一下，我们把这个查询向量写成 q。之后你看到我把一个矩阵放在这样的箭头旁边时，它表示用这个矩阵乘以箭头起点的向量，就得到箭头终点的向量。

cues.en: In this case, you multiply this matrix by all of the embeddings in the context producing one query vector for each token.
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，你用这个矩阵乘以上下文中所有的嵌入，为每个 token 生成一个查询向量。

cues.en: The entries of this matrix are parameters of the model, which means the true behavior is learned from data. And in practice, what this matrix does in a particular attention head is challenging to parse. But for our sake, imagining an example that we might hope that it would learn, we'll suppose that this query matrix maps the embeddings of nouns to certain directions in this smaller query space that somehow encodes the notion of looking for adjectives in preceding positions.
cues.zh: 这个矩阵的元素是模型的参数，也就是说真实行为是从数据中学到的。而在实践中，这个矩阵在某个特定的注意力头里到底做什么，是很难解析的。但为了我们的讨论，想象一个我们可能希望它学会的例子，我们假设这个查询矩阵把名词的嵌入映射到这个小查询空间中的某些方向，这些方向以某种方式编码了“在前面的位置寻找形容词”这一概念。

cues.en: As to what it does to other embeddings, who knows? Maybe it simultaneously tries to accomplish some other goal with those. Right now, we're laser focused on the nouns.
cues.zh: 至于它对其他嵌入做了什么，谁知道呢？也许它同时在用那些嵌入尝试实现别的什么目标。现在我们只把注意力死死盯在名词上。

cues.en: At the same time, associated with this is a second matrix called the key matrix,
cues.zh: 与此同时，与之相关的是一个称为键矩阵的第二个矩阵，

cues.en: which you also multiply by every one of the embeddings.
cues.zh: 你同样要将它与每一个嵌入向量相乘。

cues.en: This produces a second sequence of vectors that we call the keys.
cues.zh: 这会生成第二个向量序列，我们称之为键。

cues.en: Conceptually,
cues.zh: 从概念上讲，

cues.en: you wanna think of the keys as potentially answering the queries.
cues.zh: 你可以把键理解为对查询的潜在回应。

cues.en: This key matrix is also full of tunable parameters, and just like the query matrix, it maps the embedding vectors to that same smaller dimensional space.
cues.zh: 这个键矩阵同样充满了可调参数，就像查询矩阵一样，它把嵌入向量映射到同一个更小的维度空间。

cues.en: You think of the keys as matching the queries whenever they closely align with each other. In our example, you would imagine that the key matrix maps the adjectives,
cues.zh: 你可以把键理解为与查询相匹配——只要它们彼此紧密对齐。在我们的例子中，你可以想象键矩阵会把形容词

cues.en: like fluffy and blue, to vectors that are closely aligned with the query produced by the word creature.
cues.zh: 比如 fluffy 和 blue，映射到与单词 creature 产生的查询紧密对齐的向量。

cues.en: To measure how well each key matches each query, you compute a dot product between each possible key query pair.
cues.zh: 为了衡量每个键与每个查询的匹配程度，你需要计算每一对可能的键-查询之间的点积。

cues.en: I like to visualize a grid full of a bunch of dots where the bigger dots correspond to the larger dot products, the places where the keys and queries align.
cues.zh: 我喜欢把它可视化为一个布满许多点的网格，其中较大的点对应较大的点积，也就是键和查询对齐的地方。

cues.en: For our adjective noun example, that would look a little more like this
cues.zh: 对于我们的形容词-名词例子，那看起来会更像这样

cues.en: where if the keys produced by fluffy and blue really do align closely with the query produced by creature,
cues.zh: 如果 fluffy 和 blue 产生的键确实与 creature 产生的查询紧密对齐，

cues.en: then the dot products in these two spots would be some large positive numbers.
cues.zh: 那么这两个位置上的点积就会是较大的正数。

cues.en: In the lingo, machine learning people would say that this means the embeddings of fluffy and blue attend to the embedding of creature.
cues.zh: 用行话说，机器学习的人会说，这意味着 fluffy 和 blue 的嵌入关注到了 creature 的嵌入。

cues.en: By contrast to the dot product between the key for some other word like the and the query for creature would be some small or negative value that reflects that these are unrelated to each other.
cues.zh: 相比之下，比如像 the 这个词的键与 creature 的查询之间的点积，则会是一个很小或为负的值，这反映出这两个词彼此毫无关联。

cues.en: So we have this grid of values that can be any real number from negative infinity to infinity,
cues.zh: 所以我们得到了一个由实数组成的数值网格，这些实数可以是负无穷到正无穷之间的任意值，

cues.en: giving us a score for how relevant each word is to updating the meaning of every other word.
cues.zh: 从而得出每个词对于更新其他所有词的含义而言有多大相关性的评分。

cues.en: The way we're about to use these scores is to take a certain weighted sum along each column
cues.zh: 我们即将使用这些评分的方式是，在每一列上计算一个特定的加权和，

cues.en: weighted by the relevance.
cues.zh: 权值就是相关性。

cues.en: So instead of having values range from negative infinity to infinity,
cues.zh: 所以这些值不再是处于负无穷到正无穷的范围内，

cues.en: what we want is for the numbers in these columns to be between zero and one, and for each column to add up to one as if they were a probability distribution.
cues.zh: 而是希望这些列中的数字介于 0 和 1 之间，并且每列加起来等于 1，就像概率分布那样。

cues.en: If you're coming in from the last chapter, you know what we need to do then. We compute a softmax along each one of these columns to normalize the values.
cues.zh: 如果你看过上一章，就知道我们接下来该做什么了。我们沿每一列计算 softmax 来对这些值进行归一化。

cues.en: In our picture, after you apply softmax to all of the columns, we'll fill in the grid with these normalized values.
cues.zh: 在我们的图示中，对所有列应用 softmax 之后，我们会用这些归一化后的值来填充网格。

cues.en: At this point, you're safe to think about each column as giving weights according to how relevant the word on the left is to the corresponding value at the top. We call this grid an attention pattern.
cues.zh: 此时，你可以理所当然地认为，每一列都根据左侧的词与顶部对应值的相关性给出了权重。我们将这个网格称为注意力模式。

cues.en: Now if you look at the original transformer paper, there's a really compact way that they write this all down.
cues.zh: 现在，如果你去看最初的 Transformer 论文，会发现他们有一种非常简洁的方式把这一切写下来。

cues.en: Here, the variables q and k represent the full arrays of query and key vectors respectively,
cues.zh: 这里，变量 q 和 k 分别代表 query 和 key 向量的完整数组，

cues.en: those little vectors you get by multiplying the embeddings by the query and the key matrices.
cues.zh: 那些小向量，就是把嵌入乘以查询矩阵和键矩阵后得到的。

cues.en: This expression up in the numerator is a really compact way to represent the grid of all possible dot products between pairs of keys and queries.
cues.zh: 分子上的这个表达式，是表示键和查询之间所有可能点积网格的一种非常紧凑的方式。

cues.en: A small technical detail that I didn't mention is that for numerical stability,
cues.zh: 我没有提及的一个微小技术细节是，为了数值稳定性，

cues.en: it happens to be helpful to divide all of these values by the square root of the dimension in that key query space.
cues.zh: 事实证明，把这些值都除以该 key query 空间中维度的平方根会很有帮助。

cues.en: Then this softmax that's wrapped around the full expression is meant to be understood to apply column by column.
cues.zh: 然后，包裹在整个表达式外面的这个 softmax，需要理解为是按列应用的。

cues.en: As to that v term, we'll talk about it in just a second. Before that, there's one other technical detail that so far I've skipped. During the training process, when you run this model on a given text example, and all of the weights are slightly adjusted and tuned to either reward or punish it based on how high a probability it assigns to the true next word in the passage,
cues.zh: 至于那个 v 项，我们马上就会讲到。在此之前，还有一个技术细节我刚才跳过了。在训练过程中，当你用这个模型处理给定的文本样本时，所有的权重都会被微调，根据它为文章中真正的下一个词分配的概率有多高来给予奖励或惩罚，

cues.en: it turns out to make the whole training process a lot more efficient if you simultaneously
cues.zh: 事实证明，如果同时进行，整个训练过程会高效得多。

cues.en: have it predict every possible next token following each initial subsequence of tokens in this passage.
cues.zh: 让它为该段落中每个初始 token 子序列预测所有可能的下一个 token。

cues.en: For example, with the phrase that we've been focusing on, it might also be predicting what words follow creature and what words follow the.
cues.zh: 例如，对于我们一直关注的这个短语，它可能还会预测 creature 后面会跟什么词，以及 the 后面会跟什么词。

cues.en: This is really nice because it means what would otherwise be a single training example effectively acts as many.
cues.zh: 这一点非常好，因为它意味着原本单个训练样本实际上能起到多个样本的作用。

cues.en: For the purposes of our attention pattern, it means that you never want to allow later words to influence earlier words since otherwise they could kind of give away the answer for what comes next.
cues.zh: 就我们的注意力模式而言，这意味着你绝不能让后面的词影响前面的词，否则它们就可能泄露下一个词的答案。

cues.en: What this means is that we want all of these spots here, the ones representing later tokens influencing earlier ones,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们希望这里所有这些位置，也就是代表后面 token 影响前面 token 的位置，

cues.en: to somehow be forced to be zero.
cues.zh: 都被强制设为零。

cues.en: The simplest thing you might think to do is to set them equal to zero, but if you did that, the columns wouldn't add up to one anymore. They wouldn't be normalized.
cues.zh: 你最先想到的最简单做法可能是把它们设为零，但这样一来，列就不再相加等于一了，它们就不再归一化了。

cues.en: So instead, a common way to do this is that before applying softmax,
cues.zh: 所以，常见的做法是在应用 softmax 之前，

cues.en: you set all of those entries to be negative infinity.
cues.zh: 把所有这些项设为负无穷。

cues.en: If you do that, then after applying softmax,
cues.zh: 这样做之后，再应用 softmax，

cues.en: all of those get turned into zero, but the columns stay normalized.
cues.zh: 这些项就都变成零了，但列仍然保持归一化。

cues.en: This process is called masking.
cues.zh: 这个过程叫做掩码。

cues.en: There are versions of attention where you don't apply it, but in our GPT example, even though this is more relevant during the training phase than it would be, say, running it as a chatbot or something like that, you do always apply this masking to prevent later tokens from influencing earlier ones.
cues.zh: 有些注意力变体不应用它，但在我们的 GPT 示例中，虽然这在训练阶段比在作为聊天机器人运行等场景中更相关，但你始终要应用这个掩码，以防止后面的 token 影响前面的 token。

cues.en: Another fact that's worth reflecting on about this attention pattern is how its size is equal to the square of the context size. So this is why context size can be a really huge bottleneck for large language models, and scaling it up is nontrivial.
cues.zh: 关于这个注意力模式，另一个值得思考的事实是它的大小等于上下文长度的平方。所以这就是为什么上下文长度会成为大语言模型的一个巨大瓶颈，而扩展它绝非易事。

cues.en: As you might imagine, motivated by a desire for bigger and bigger context windows, recent years have seen some variations to the attention mechanism aimed at making context more scalable. But right here, you and I are staying focused on the basics.
cues.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，出于对越来越大的上下文窗口的渴望，近年来注意力机制出现了一些变体，旨在让上下文更具可扩展性。但在这里，你和我将专注于基础知识。

cues.en: Okay. Great. Computing this pattern lets the model deduce which words are relevant to which other words.
cues.zh: 好的。太棒了。计算出这种模式可以让模型推断出哪些词与哪些其他词相关。

cues.en: Now you need to actually update the embeddings,
cues.zh: 现在你需要实际更新嵌入，

cues.en: allowing words to pass information to whichever other words they're relevant to. For example, you want the embedding of fluffy to somehow cause a change to creature that moves it to a different part of this 12,000 dimensional embedding space that more specifically encodes a fluffy creature.
cues.zh: 允许词语将信息传递给与它们相关的任何其他词。例如，你希望 fluffy 的 embedding 能以某种方式引发 creature 的改变，使其移动到这个 12,000 维 embedding 空间的另一个部分，从而更具体地编码“毛茸茸的生物”这一概念。

cues.en: What I'm gonna do here is first show you the most straightforward way that you could do this, though there's a slight way that this gets modified in the context of multi headed attention.
cues.zh: 我接下来要做的是，首先向你展示最直接的实现方式，尽管在多头注意力机制（multi-headed attention）的语境下，这种方式会被稍微修改一下。

cues.en: This most straightforward way would be to use a third matrix, what we call the value matrix,
cues.zh: 这种最直接的方式是使用第三个矩阵，也就是我们所说的值矩阵（value matrix），

cues.en: which you multiply by the embedding of that first word, for example, fluffy.
cues.zh: 你用它乘以第一个词的 embedding，比如 fluffy。

cues.en: The result of this is what you would call a value vector,
cues.zh: 这个操作的结果就是所谓的价值向量（value vector），

cues.en: and this is something that you add to the embedding of the second word. In this case, something you add to the embedding of creature.
cues.zh: 这就是你要加到第二个词的 embedding 上的东西。在这个例子中，就是加到 creature 的 embedding 上。

cues.en: So this value vector lives in the same very high dimensional space as the embeddings.
cues.zh: 因此，这个价值向量和 embedding 处于同一个超高维空间中。

cues.en: When you multiply this value matrix by the embedding of a word, you might think of it as saying,
cues.zh: 当你用某个词的嵌入去乘这个值矩阵时，可以把它理解为在说：

cues.en: if this word is relevant to adjusting the meaning of something else,
cues.zh: 如果这个词与调整其他词的含义有关，

cues.en: what exactly should be added to the embedding of that something else in order to reflect this?
cues.zh: 那到底应该往那个词的嵌入里加上什么，才能体现这种关系？

cues.en: Looking back in our diagram,
cues.zh: 回看我们的示意图，

cues.en: let's set aside all of the keys and the queries since after you compute the attention pattern, you're done with those. Then you're gonna take this value matrix and multiply it by every one of those embeddings to produce a sequence of value vectors.
cues.zh: 先把所有键和查询放到一边，因为算完注意力模式后，它们就用不上了。然后你要拿这个值矩阵，去乘每一个嵌入，生成一串值向量。

cues.en: You might think of these value vectors as being kind of associated with the corresponding keys.
cues.zh: 你可以把这些值向量看作与对应的键有些关联。

cues.en: For each column in this diagram,
cues.zh: 对于这张图里的每一列，

cues.en: you multiply each of the value vectors by the corresponding weight in that column.
cues.zh: 你把每个值向量乘以该列中对应的权重。

cues.en: For example, here, under the embedding of creature, you would be adding large proportions of the value vectors for fluffy and blue, while all of the other value vectors get zeroed out or at least nearly zeroed out. And then finally, the way to actually update the embedding associated with this column, previously encoding some context free meaning of creature, you add together all of these rescaled values in the column producing a change that you want to add that I'll label delta e,
cues.zh: 例如这里，在 creature 的嵌入下面，你会加入很大比例的 fluffy 和 blue 的值向量，而所有其他值向量会被清零，或至少接近清零。最后，要真正更新这一列对应的嵌入——它之前编码的是 creature 某种上下文无关的含义——你把这一列里所有重新缩放后的值加起来，得到一个你想加上的变化，我把它记作 delta e，

cues.en: and then you add that to the original embedding.
cues.zh: 然后把它加到原始嵌入上。

cues.en: Hopefully, what results is a more refined vector encoding the more contextually rich meaning like that of a fluffy blue creature.
cues.zh: 希望得到的是一个更精细的向量，编码出更丰富的上下文含义，比如一只毛茸茸的蓝色小生物。

cues.en: And, of course, you don't just do this to one embedding, you apply the same weighted sum across all of the columns in this picture producing a sequence of changes.
cues.zh: 当然，你不只对一个嵌入这样做，而是对图中所有列应用同样的加权求和，生成一系列变化。

cues.en: Adding all of those changes to the corresponding embeddings produces a full sequence of more refined embeddings popping out of the attention block.
cues.zh: 把所有这些变化加到对应的嵌入上，就会从注意力模块中输出一整个序列的更精细的嵌入。

cues.en: Zooming out, this whole process is what you would describe as a single head of attention.
cues.zh: 从整体来看，整个过程就是所谓的单个注意力头。

cues.en: As I've described things so far, this process is parameterized by three distinct matrices,
cues.zh: 就我目前描述的内容而言，这个过程由三个不同的矩阵参数化，

cues.en: all filled with tunable parameters,
cues.zh: 全都充满了可调参数，

cues.en: the key, the query, and the value.
cues.zh: 即键、查询和值。

cues.en: I wanna take a moment to continue what we started in the last chapter with the score keeping where we count up the total number of model parameters using the numbers from GPT three.
cues.zh: 我想花点时间继续上一章开始的工作，也就是记录分数，用GPT-3的数字来统计模型参数的总数。

cues.en: These key and query matrices each have 12,288
cues.zh: 这些键矩阵和查询矩阵各有12,288

cues.en: columns matching the embedding dimension and 128
cues.zh: 列，与嵌入维度匹配，还有128

cues.en: rows matching the dimension of that smaller key query space.
cues.zh: 行，与那个更小的键查询空间的维度匹配。

cues.en: This gives us an additional 1,500,000
cues.zh: 这给我们每个矩阵额外增加了大约1,500,000

cues.en: or so parameters for each one. If you look at that value matrix by contrast, the way I've described things so far would suggest that it's a square matrix that has 12,288
cues.zh: 个参数。相比之下，如果你看那个值矩阵，按我目前的描述方式，它应该是一个方阵，有12,288

cues.en: columns and 12,288
rows since both its inputs and its outputs live in this very large embedding space.
cues.zh: 行，因为它的输入和输出都位于这个非常大的嵌入空间中。

cues.en: If true, that would mean about a 150,000,000
cues.zh: 如果真是这样，那就意味着大约增加了150,000,000

cues.en: added parameters.
cues.zh: 个参数。

cues.en: And to be clear, you could do that. You could devote orders of magnitude more parameters to the value map than to the key in query. But in practice, it is much more efficient if instead you make it so that the number of parameters devoted to this value map is the same as the number devoted to the key in the query.
cues.zh: 说清楚一点，你确实可以这样做。你可以把比键和查询多几个数量级的参数分配给值映射。但在实践中，如果你让分配给这个值映射的参数数量与分配给键和查询的参数数量相同，效率会高得多。

cues.en: This is especially relevant in the setting of running multiple attention heads in parallel.
cues.zh: 这在并行运行多个注意力头（attention head）的场景下尤为相关。

cues.en: The way this looks is that the value map is factored as a product of two smaller matrices.
cues.zh: 具体来说，这里的 value 映射被分解成了两个较小矩阵的乘积。

cues.en: Conceptually, I would still encourage you to think about the overall linear map, one with inputs and outputs both in this larger embedding space, For example, taking the embedding of blue to this blueness direction that you would add to nouns. It's just that it's broken up into two separate steps.
cues.zh: 从概念上讲，我还是建议大家把整体的线性映射当作一个整体来思考，它的输入和输出都在这个更大的嵌入空间中。例如，将“蓝色”的嵌入映射到会叠加到名词上的“蓝度”方向。只不过它被拆成了两个独立的步骤。

cues.en: The first matrix on the right here has a smaller number of rows, typically the same size as the key query space. What this means is you can think of it as mapping the large embedding vectors down to a much smaller space.
cues.zh: 这里右侧的第一个矩阵行数较少，通常和 key-query 空间的大小相同。这意味着你可以把它看作是将大型嵌入向量映射到一个小得多的空间。

cues.en: This is not the conventional naming, but I'm gonna call this the value down matrix.
cues.zh: 这不是常规的命名，但我打算叫它 value down 矩阵。

cues.en: The second matrix maps from this smaller space back up to the embedding space, producing the vectors that you use to make the actual updates. I'm gonna call this one the value up matrix,
cues.zh: 第二个矩阵将这个较小的空间重新映射回嵌入空间，生成用于实际更新的向量。我打算叫它 value up 矩阵，

cues.en: which again is not conventional.
cues.zh: 当然，这也不是常规叫法。

cues.en: The way that you would see this written in most papers looks a little different. I'll talk about it in a minute. In my opinion, it tends to make things a little more conceptually confusing.
cues.zh: 你在大多数论文里看到的写法会略有不同。我一会儿就会讲到。但在我看来，那往往会让概念变得更难理解。

cues.en: To throw in linear algebra jargon here, what we're basically doing is constraining the overall value map to be a low rank transformation.
cues.zh: 用线性代数术语来说，我们基本上就是在约束整体的 value 映射为一个低秩变换。

cues.en: Turning back to the parameter count, all four of these matrices have the same size, and adding them all up, we get about 6,300,000
cues.zh: 回到参数量上来，这四个矩阵的大小都一样，把它们全加起来，我们大约会得到 6,300,000 个

cues.en: parameters
cues.zh: 参数

cues.en: for one attention head.
cues.zh: 属于一个 attention head。

cues.en: As a quick side note, to be a little more accurate, everything described so far is what people would call a self attention head to distinguish it from a variation that comes up in other models that's called cross attention.
cues.zh: 顺便提一下，严格来说，目前为止描述的所有内容就是大家所说的 self attention head，这是为了把它和另一种在其他模型中出现的变体——cross attention 区分开来。

cues.en: This isn't relevant to our GPT example,
cues.zh: 这和我们的 GPT 示例没有关系，

cues.en: but if you're curious, cross attention involves models that process two distinct types of data, like text in one language and text in another language that's part of an ongoing generation of a translation,
cues.zh: 但如果你好奇的话，cross attention 涉及处理两种不同类型数据的模型，比如一种语言的文本和另一种正在生成的翻译文本，

cues.en: or maybe audio input of speech and an ongoing transcription.
cues.zh: 或者可能是语音的音频输入和正在进行的转写。

cues.en: A cross attention head looks almost identical. The only difference is that the key and query maps act on different datasets.
cues.zh: cross attention head 看起来几乎一模一样，唯一的区别是 key 矩阵和 query 矩阵作用于不同的数据集。

cues.en: In a model doing translation,
cues.zh: 例如在做翻译的模型中，

cues.en: for example, the keys might come from one language while the queries come from another, and the attention pattern could describe which words from one language correspond to which words in another.
cues.zh: key 可能来自一种语言，而 query 来自另一种，注意力模式则可以描述一种语言中的哪些词对应另一种语言中的哪些词。

cues.en: And in this setting, there would typically be no masking since there's not really any notion of later tokens affecting earlier ones.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，通常不会有掩码（masking），因为这里其实不存在后面的 token 影响前面 token 的概念。

cues.en: Staying focused on self attention though, if you understood everything so far and if you were to stop here, you would come away with the essence of what attention really is.
cues.zh: 不过把重点回到 self attention 上，如果你理解了目前为止的内容，并且在这里停下来，你就已经掌握了 attention 的真正精髓。

cues.en: All that's really left to us is to lay out the sense in which you do this many, different times.
cues.zh: 留给我们真正要做的，就是阐明你是如何多次、从不同层面来做这件事的。

cues.en: In our central example, we focused on adjectives updating nouns, but of course, there are lots of different ways that context can influence the meaning of a word. If the words they crashed thee preceded the word car, it has implications for the shape and the structure of that car.
cues.zh: 在我们的核心示例中，重点关注的是形容词修饰名词，但当然，上下文影响词义的方式有很多种。如果在单词 car 之前出现了 crashed thee，这会影响到这辆车的形状和结构。

cues.en: And a lot of associations might be less grammatical.
cues.zh: 而且许多关联可能没那么符合语法。

cues.en: If the word wizard is anywhere in the same passage as Harry, it suggests that this might be referring to Harry Potter. Whereas if instead the words queen, Sussex, and William were in that passage,
cues.zh: 如果 wizard 这个词与 Harry 出现在同一段落中，这就暗示它可能指的是哈利·波特。而如果在该段落中出现的是 queen、Sussex 和 William 这些词，

cues.en: then perhaps the embedding of Harry should instead be updated to refer to the prince.
cues.zh: 那么 Harry 的嵌入表示或许就应该更新为指代这位王子。

cues.en: For every different type of contextual updating that you might imagine, the parameters of these key and query matrices would be different to capture the different attention patterns, and the parameters of our value map would be different based on what should be added to the embeddings.
cues.zh: 对于你能想象到的每一种不同类型的上下文更新，这些键和查询矩阵的参数都会不同，以捕获不同的注意力模式，并且价值映射的参数也会根据应该向嵌入中添加什么内容而有所不同。

cues.en: And again, in practice, the true behavior of these maps is much more difficult to interpret, where the weights are set to do whatever the model needs them to do to best accomplish its goal of predicting the next token.
cues.zh: 再说一次，在实践中，这些映射的真实行为要难解释得多，权重被设置为模型实现其预测下一个 token 目标所需的任何状态。

cues.en: As I said before, everything we described is a single head of attention, and a full attention block inside a transformer consists of what's called multi headed attention, where you run a lot of these operations in parallel,
cues.zh: 正如我之前所说，我们刚才描述的一切都只是单个注意力头，而 transformer 内部的一个完整注意力块由所谓的“多头注意力”组成，即并行运行许多这样的操作，

cues.en: each with its own distinct key query and value maps.
cues.zh: 每一个操作都有其独特的键、查询和价值映射。

cues.en: GPT three, for example, uses 96 attention heads inside each block. Considering that each one is already a bit confusing, it's certainly a lot to hold in your head. Just to spell it all out very explicitly,
cues.zh: 比如 GPT-3，在每个块内部使用了 96 个注意力头。考虑到每一个本身就已经有点让人迷惑了，要全盘记住它们确实很不容易。为了把它讲得更明白一点，

cues.en: this means you have 96 distinct key and query matrices
cues.zh: 这意味着你有 96 个不同的键矩阵和查询矩阵，

cues.en: producing 96 distinct attention patterns.
cues.zh: 从而产生 96 种不同的注意力模式。

cues.en: Then each head has its own distinct value matrices
cues.zh: 然后，每个头都有自己独立的值矩阵，

cues.en: used to produce 96 sequences of value vectors.
cues.zh: 用于生成 96 个值向量序列。

cues.en: These are all added together using the corresponding attention patterns as weights.
cues.zh: 这些向量会通过对应的注意力模式作为权重全部相加在一起。

cues.en: What this means is that for each position in the context,
cues.zh: 这意味着对于上下文中的每个位置，

cues.en: each token, every one of these heads produces a proposed change to be added to the embedding in that position.
cues.zh: 每个 Token，所有这些头中的每一个都会产生一个建议的改动，用来加到该位置的嵌入中。

cues.en: So what you do is you sum together all of those proposed changes, one for each head, and you add the result to the original embedding of that position.
cues.zh: 所以你要做的是，把所有这些建议的改动加总起来（每个头一个），然后把结果加到该位置的原始嵌入上。

cues.en: This entire sum here would be one slice of what's outputted from this multi headed attention block, a single one of those refined embeddings that pops out the other end of it.
cues.zh: 这里的整个求和结果，就是多头注意力块输出的一个切片，也就是从另一端蹦出来的那些精炼嵌入中的一个。

cues.en: Again, this is a lot to think about, so don't worry at all if it takes some time to sink in. The overall idea is that by running many distinct heads in parallel,
cues.zh: 再说一次，这需要思考的内容很多，所以如果需要花点时间才能理解，完全不用担心。整体的思路是，通过并行运行许多不同的头，

cues.en: you're giving the model the capacity
cues.zh: 你赋予了模型这种能力：

cues.en: to learn many distinct ways that context changes meaning.
cues.zh: 去学习上下文改变意义的许多不同方式。

cues.en: Pulling up our running tally for parameter count with 96 heads each including its own variation of these four matrices,
cues.zh: 拿出我们一直在统计的参数量，在拥有 96 个头且每个头都包含这四个矩阵的各自变体的情况下，

cues.en: each block of multi headed attention ends up with around 600,000,000
cues.zh: 每个多头注意力块最终大约有 6 亿个

cues.en: parameters.
cues.zh: 参数。

cues.en: There's one added slightly annoying thing that I should really mention for any of you who go on to read more about transformers.
cues.zh: 还有一点稍显繁琐的细节，如果大家之后要阅读更多关于 Transformer 的资料，我必须提一下。

cues.en: You remember how I said that the value map is factored out into these two distinct matrices,
cues.zh: 还记得我说过，Value 映射被分解成了两个独立的矩阵吗，

cues.en: which I labeled as the value down and the value up matrices.
cues.zh: 也就是我标记为 Value Down 和 Value Up 的矩阵。

cues.en: The way that I framed things would suggest that you see this pair of matrices inside each attention head,
cues.zh: 按照我之前的说法，每个注意力头内部好像都有这样一对矩阵，

cues.en: and you could absolutely implement it this way. That would be a valid design. But the way that you see this written in papers and the way that it's implemented in practice looks a little different. All of these value up matrices for each head appear stapled together in one giant matrix that we call the output matrix associated with the entire multi headed attention block. And when you see people refer to the value matrix for a given attention head, they're typically only referring to this first step, the one that I was labeling as the value down projection into the smaller space.
cues.zh: 你完全可以这么实现，这种设计也没问题。但在论文和实际实现中，形式会稍有不同。每个头的所有 Value Up 矩阵其实都被拼接在了一起，形成一个巨大的矩阵，也就是整个多头注意力模块所对应的输出矩阵（output matrix）。当大家提到某个特定注意力头的 Value 矩阵时，通常只指第一步，即我标记为向较小空间投影的 Value Down 矩阵。

cues.en: For the curious among you, I've left an on screen note about it. It's one of those details that runs the risk of distracting from the main conceptual points, but I do wanna call it out just so that you know if you read about this in other sources.
cues.zh: 感兴趣的同学可以看屏幕上的注释。这类细节容易让人偏离核心概念，但我还是想指出来，免得大家在阅读其他资料时感到困惑。

cues.en: Setting aside all the technical nuances, in the preview from the last chapter, we saw how data flowing through a transformer
cues.zh: 撇开这些技术细节不谈，在上一章的预览中，我们已经看到数据在流经 Transformer 时，

cues.en: doesn't just flow through a single attention block.
cues.zh: 并不仅仅只穿过一个注意力模块。

cues.en: For one thing, it also goes through these other operations called multilayer perceptrons.
cues.zh: 一方面，它还会经过这些称为多层感知机的其他运算。

cues.en: We'll talk more about those in the next chapter. And then it repeatedly goes through many, many copies of both of these operations.
cues.zh: 关于这些，我们会在下一章深入讨论。接着，它会反复执行这两种操作的大量副本。

cues.en: What this means is that after a given word imbibes some of its context, there are many more chances for this more nuanced embedding to be influenced by its more nuanced surroundings.
cues.zh: 这意味着在一个给定的词吸收了部分上下文之后，这个更加微妙的嵌入将有更多机会被它周围同样微妙的环境所影响。

cues.en: The further down the network you go, with each embedding taking in more and more meaning from all the other embeddings, which themselves are getting more and more nuanced, the hope is that there's the capacity to encode higher level and more abstract ideas about a given input beyond just descriptors and grammatical structure.
cues.zh: 随着网络层层深入，每个嵌入向量从其他所有嵌入向量中吸收越来越多的含义，而这些嵌入向量本身也变得越来越细腻微妙，人们希望它有能力对给定输入的更高级、更抽象的概念进行编码，而不仅仅是描述词和语法结构。

cues.en: Things like sentiment and tone and whether it's a poem and what underlying scientific truths are relevant to the piece and things like that.
cues.zh: 比如情感和语气、它是不是一首诗、哪些底层科学真理与这篇作品相关，诸如此类。

cues.en: Turning back one more time to our scorekeeping,
cues.zh: 再回到我们的记分系统，

cues.en: g p t three includes 96 distinct layers,
cues.zh: GPT-3 包含 96 个不同的层，

cues.en: so the total number of key query and value parameters is multiplied by another 96,
cues.zh: 所以 key、query 和 value 参数的总数还要再乘以 96，

cues.en: which brings the total sum to just under 58,000,000,000
cues.zh: 这使得总和刚好不到580亿

cues.en: distinct parameters devoted to all of the attention heads. That is a lot to be sure, but it's only about a third of the 175,000,000,000
cues.zh: 专属于所有注意力头的独立参数。这确实是一个很大的数字，但也只占那 175,000,000,000 大约三分之一

cues.en: that are in the network in total.
cues.zh: 也就是网络中总共的那些。

cues.en: So even though attention gets all of the attention, the majority of parameters come from the blocks sitting in between these steps. In the next chapter, you and I will talk more about those other blocks and also a lot more about the training process.
cues.zh:
所以尽管 Attention 备受关注，但绝大多数参数实际上都来自于这些步骤之间的模块。
@@
在下一章中，你和我将深入探讨那些其他模块，还会详细讨论训练过程。

cues.en: A big part of the story for the success of the attention mechanism
cues.zh: 注意力机制成功的关键

cues.en: is not so much any specific kind of behavior that it enables,
cues.zh: 并不在于它启用了某种特定的行为，

cues.en: but the fact that it's extremely parallelizable,
cues.zh: 而在于它极度可并行化，

cues.en: meaning that you can run a huge number of computations in a short time using GPUs.
cues.zh: 这意味着你可以在短时间内用 GPU 运行大量计算。

cues.en: Given that one of the big lessons about deep learning in the last decade or two has been that scale alone seems to give huge qualitative improvements in model performance, there's a huge advantage to parallelizable architectures that let you do this.
cues.zh: 鉴于过去一二十年深度学习的一大教训是，仅凭规模似乎就能给模型性能带来巨大的质的提升，因此可并行化的架构能让你做到这一点，具有巨大的优势。

cues.zh: 如果你想了解更多这方面的内容，我在描述里留了很多链接。

But if you're curious about more of the history for how we got here and how you might reinvent this idea for yourself, my friend Vivek just put up a couple videos giving a lot more of that motivation.
cues.zh: 特别是 Andre Karpathy 或 Chris Ola 制作的任何内容往往是纯金。在这个视频里，我只想直接进入当前形式的注意力机制。但如果你好奇更多我们如何走到这一步的历史，以及你如何自己重新发明这个想法，我的朋友 Vivek 刚发了几个视频，给出了更多那样的动机。
